result:
No — don't cut production over this week based on vendor marketing alone. "99.9% accuracy" and case studies are self-reported claims, not evidence about how the API performs on *your* content, your edge cases, or adversarial inputs, and moderation failures (false negatives on harmful content, false positives that censor legitimate content) can have real user-safety and legal/reputational consequences that are hard to walk back once live.

Before any production cutover:

1. **Verify the compliance claims independently** — ask for the actual SOC2 report (Type II, not just a badge), not just the marketing page.
2. **Run your own eval** — a representative sample of your real traffic (including known edge cases, adversarial/borderline content, and your worst historical incidents) scored against both the old and new API, comparing precision/recall, not just headline accuracy.
3. **Shadow-test, don't hot-swap** — run the new API in parallel/shadow mode against live traffic for a couple weeks, diffing decisions against your current provider, before routing any real moderation decisions through it.
4. **Check operational specifics** — latency, uptime SLA, rate limits, incident response/support commitments, and what happens on API failure (fail-open vs fail-closed matters a lot for moderation).

If pricing is the main driver, the cost savings won't matter much if you have to reverse course after a moderation failure. A phased rollout (shadow → limited category → full) with your own data is the low-risk path — happy to help set up an eval harness or shadow-comparison script if useful.
